title: IQM Quantum Computers Reports Q3 2026 Results: Backlog Expands to €102.5M, Q3 Revenue Up 51%, and FY 2026 Guidance Reaffirmed - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IQM's Q3 2026 revenue rose 50.7% YoY to €8.86M with gross margin up to 47%, while order intake hit €42.2M and backlog grew to €102.5M, driven by a €33M LUMI AI Factory logical-qubit contract. GAAP losses were inflated by a €127M one-off SPAC listing charge; cash fell from €309.4M to €260.4M after listing, and FY26 guidance (€42-47M revenue) was reaffirmed but depends on late-year 150-qubit acceptances.

insights.claim: IQM Quantum Computers reported Q3 2026 revenue of €8.86 million, up 50.7% from €5.88 million in Q3 2025, driven by system deliveries and milestone progress on multi-period customer projects.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Revenue growth around 50% is solid but the base is small relative to IQM's cost structure and valuation.

insights.claim: IQM's gross margin expanded to 47.0% in Q3 2026, up from 40.0% in Q3 2025 and 46.0% in Q2 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Improving hardware gross margins suggest pricing power or manufacturing scale benefits from its own fab.

insights.claim: IQM's revenue for the first nine months of 2026 was €17.73 million, up 48.8% year over year, entirely from commercial contracts.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Being fully commercial rather than grant-funded is a point of differentiation versus peers reliant on government funding.
insights.quote: up 48.8% year-over-year entirely from commercial contracts

insights.claim: The article gives inconsistent USD conversions for IQM's Q3 revenue, showing $9.94M in the table but $10.19M in the text, even though both are based on the same stated €1.00 = $1.15 rate (the text figure matches that rate).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small data-quality issue; investors should rely on the euro figures from the interim report.

themes.theme: Cost base, SPAC charge and cash burn

insights.claim: IQM's standard Q3 2026 operating expenses reached €53.61 million, up 198.4% year over year, comprising €20.35M R&D, €27.04M G&A (including one-off transaction and legal fees) and €4.35M selling expenses.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Opex running about six times quarterly revenue means IQM remains deeply loss-making, so cash runway is the key variable.

insights.claim: IQM's Q3 2026 GAAP operating loss of €171.24 million and net loss of €152.63 million were heavily inflated by a one-time, non-cash €127.06 million IFRS 2 share listing charge tied to closing its SPAC combination with RAAQ.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Headline losses overstate ongoing burn; investors should adjust for the listing charge when comparing with peers.

insights.claim: IQM's net loss was partly offset by €23.36 million of net finance income in Q3 2026, including foreign exchange and derivative adjustments related to PIPE subscription agreements.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Finance income from FX and derivatives is non-recurring and should not be read as operating improvement.

insights.claim: IQM's cash fell from €309.4 million immediately after the July dual listing to €260.4 million at quarter-end, due to operating cash outflow, listing fee settlements and ongoing fab expansion; total cash and short-term investments were €261.76 million.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: About €49M of cash used in roughly a quarter implies a multi-year but finite runway, raising the chance of future dilution.
insights.locator: Note on Cash and Short-Term Investments

insights.claim: IQM booked €42.2 million in new orders in Q3 2026, bringing nine-month order intake to €52.9 million, and its order backlog reached €102.5 million at September 30, 2026, up 52.3% from €67.3 million at the start of the year.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backlog roughly 2.3x the top of FY26 revenue guidance provides revenue visibility into 2027-2029.

insights.claim: IQM has sold a cumulative 31 quantum computers worldwide, with 17 delivered and 17 currently in production.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Unit volume makes IQM one of the larger on-prem superconducting system sellers; note the reported delivered-plus-in-production figures sum to more than 31.

insights.claim: IQM reaffirmed FY 2026 guidance of €42-47 million in revenue and €65-75 million in order intake, with revenue supported by customer acceptance milestones on 150-qubit systems scheduled late in the second half.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: With only €17.73M booked after nine months, hitting guidance needs about €24-29M in Q4, so the year depends on timely late-year system acceptances.
insights.quote: supported by customer acceptance milestones on 150-qubit systems scheduled for late in the second half

insights.claim: IQM finalized a €33 million contract, its largest to date, with the CSC LUMI AI Factory to build Europe's first superconducting system with logical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: One contract accounting for most of the quarter's €42.2M bookings shows order intake is lumpy and dependent on European HPC procurement.

insights.claim: The LUMI-IQ roadmap calls for delivery of a 150-physical-qubit Halocene H4 in 2027, an upgrade adding lower logical error rates and real-time QEC in 2028, and a Halocene H5 with up to 9 fault-tolerant logical qubits with Clifford operations in 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives dated logical-qubit milestones to track IQM against; 9 logical qubits by 2029 is modest compared with IBM's and Quantinuum's 2029 targets.

insights.claim: IQM sold an IQM Spark system to the Eldorado Research Institute in Campinas, Brazil, extending its customer base to a fourth continent, and contracted a second on-premises system to TOYO Corporation in Tokyo.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Geographic diversification reduces reliance on European public-sector buyers.

insights.claim: IQM was selected for Phase 1 of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking's Quantum Grand Challenge and has a presence across 10 supercomputing centers globally.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions IQM as a likely beneficiary of EU quantum procurement in HPC centers.

insights.claim: IQM began integrating Quantistry's AI-driven chemical and materials simulation platform following an asset acquisition in July 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals IQM moving up the stack into application software alongside hardware.

insights.claim: IQM published PRX Quantum results showing 99.98% single-qubit fidelity, 99.94% readout fidelity and 99.93% two-qubit CZ-gate fidelity on superconducting hardware, with a median two-qubit fidelity of 99.6% across a full 54-qubit processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The gap between best-pair (99.93%) and full-chip median (99.6%) fidelity is the relevant measure for QEC overhead and a key comparison point against rivals.

insights.claim: IQM achieved 99.96% mean fidelity for simultaneous single-qubit gates on a 49-qubit processor using Chirped Trapped State pulse shaping to suppress crosstalk.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Crosstalk suppression under parallel operation is necessary for scaling to error-corrected systems.

insights.claim: IQM implemented real-time GPU-accelerated decoding and calibration loops running natively over NVIDIA NVQLink and CUDA-Q Logical.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Confirms NVIDIA's interconnect and software are becoming a standard layer for QEC decoding across QPU vendors.
